title: Inside Michigan's most haunted asylum, 100 actors bring the nightmares to life
excerpt: Eloise Asylum's operations manager says the scares - and the paranormal activity - are very real
content:
Live In The D

Eloise Asylum’s operations manager says the scares - and the paranormal activity - are very real

Spooky season isn’t over yet, and Eloise Asylum in Westland is making sure of it. The former psychiatric hospital has been transformed into one of Michigan’s most intense haunted attractions, spread across two floors of immersive horror.

“We’re the 9th most paranormal building in the country,” said operations manager Mike Smith. “We are also one of the oldest asylums in the country. We have 2 nationally renowned haunted houses.”

The haunt leans hard into its real history. “A lot of our props and a lot of our set design is geared toward showcasing the history of the Eloise Asylum,” Smith explained during an appearance on Live in the D.

Behind the scares is a serious production operation. “We have about 100+ actors that we utilize every single night that we’re open,” he says. “A lot of our actors are from Hollywood. They do a lot of Hollywood makeup. We try to put on a state-of-the-art show that really will impress the country.”

Visitors actually get two haunted houses in one. “Our first haunted house is asylum-themed,” Smith says. “And then our second haunted house is kind of like an experimental laboratory where all the patients would go and they would run experiments on them. And that’s in our basement, which is actually one of the most paranormal floors in the entire building.”

For those who want more than a scripted scare, Eloise Asylum also runs paranormal investigations through Michigan Ghosts, whose national headquarters is based there. Sessions run from three hours up to 12-hour lockdowns inside the facility.

Smith himself didn’t start out a believer. “I never believed in ghosts until I became a partner here, and I’ve seen experiences down here as well,” he says. “It’s a crazy place.” He’s done four lockdowns so far. “Every one is a crazy experience, I will say that.”
